Early, unsigned build of Silly MIDI Tools: a native macOS app that turns audio into MIDI.

## What's new since 0.6.1

This release tidies the interface and explains two things that were hard to find.

- **Drag the MIDI file into your DAW.** The footer item now looks like a file: the MIDI file icon, "Drag into your DAW" and the file name. The pointer becomes a hand over it and it highlights, so it's clear you can pick it up and drop it onto a track in your DAW or into Finder.
- **How to use the drum separator.** Settings, Models now lists it under its own Helpers heading, with a note that says where it is switched on: pick Drums (ADTOF) or Drums (OaF, Magenta) as the model, then turn on **Separate drums first** in the inspector's Drums section.
- **No more "downloads" after you downloaded it.** The Separate drums first description used to say it downloads the 316 MB helper even when it was already on your Mac. It now says it uses the one you downloaded, and only mentions the download when it is still needed.
- **Even toolbar.** Transcribe, Save and Export are now the same height as every other toolbar button and sit on the same line. Export has its own padding and icon.
- **Steady playback controls.** Play, Stop and Loop sit closer together, the time readout no longer touches the right edge of its pill, and the pill no longer gets wider when you press Play.
- **Sidebar.** The Audio and MIDI folder paths no longer run into the right edge.

## Known limits

- Release builds are Apple silicon only, and are not notarized.
- The maintainer's Mac is Intel and cannot run this build, so the arm64 app itself has not been run by hand. The changes were checked in a Debug build on Intel, in light mode. The transport while audio is playing could not be checked, because that Mac had no audio output. Please report anything that looks wrong.
